name: donchian_channel_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Donchian channel (N-bar highest high / lowest low) breakouts capture the start of new intraday trends. Unlike moving average crossovers, Donchian is parameter-light (just one: the lookback) and doesn't whipsaw in rangebound markets because the channel only contracts, never generates false crosses. The inefficiency exists because Donchian is perceived as 'old school' and retail traders prefer fancier indicators. Not fully arbitraged because intraday Donchian requires real-time rolling max/min computation.

long.confirmation: new 30-bar high on close (not just wick)

exit.trailing_stop: exit when close crosses donchian_mid (opposite channel midline)
exit.signal_exit: exit when close crosses below donchian_mid (for longs)

filters.time_filter: no entry first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakouts aligned with nifty EMA(21) direction

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, channel breakouts are a fundamental market dynamic

weaknesses: 37% win rate is psychologically punishing. 7-10 consecutive losses are expected regularly. Most traders will override the system.
30-bar Donchian on 1-min bars = 30-minute channel. This is quite short — noise-driven breakouts will be frequent.
In rangebound markets, the channel stays tight and generates many small losses as price oscillates just above/below the channel.
prior_art: Donchian Channel Breakout. Richard Donchian (1950s). Turtle Trading System. See: Following the Trend (Clenow), Trading Evolved.
notes: The Turtle system used 20-day Donchian. Adapting to 30-min intraday is a major timeframe change. The concept is sound but the calibration needs work.
